name: Telepathy - sender (Persinger 2003 style, 6 x 5 min)
origin: Persinger lab, Laurentian University (Persinger, Koren & Tsang 2003; Persinger et al. 2010), circumcerebral 'Octopus'; phase order after the lab's six-configuration table and Murphy's Shiva 'Published Studies' session; sender/receiver trial by this project
summary: Six 5-min counter-clockwise circumcerebral configurations for the partner who wears the helmet and looks at a target, while the other, unstimulated partner in another room writes impressions. Persinger, Koren & Tsang 2003 reported 5-6 Hz EEG changes in the unstimulated partner during one configuration, which the lab describes both as 100 ms with 20-ms changes and as "20+2"; both run here, with the 100+10 rotation of its 2010 yoked study, all three first with burst-firing, then with the Thomas pulse.
notes: Changed after the primary-source check: the rotations now come from the paired-person studies themselves, replacing 20 -> 160 ms (a reading of Cook 1999) and 25 -> 11 ms (Tsang 2004). The 2003 abstract gives the effective configuration as "100 msec. with changes in rate of 20 msec." (read as 100, 120 ... 240 ms, since 100 ms cannot shorten by 20 ms seven times; the lab's Shiva study used the same ramp, Collins 2014); the lab's 2010 retelling says the effect came "when the 20+2 ms presentations occurred" and defines 20+2 as 20, 18 ... 6 ms (Persinger & Lavallee 2010, p. 793); the Swann table prints this row as "+2", and if its sign meant longer, as its "+20" must, the rotation would run 20 -> 34 ms instead. The third rotation, 100+10 (100, 90 ... 30 ms), is the one that paper gives for the 2010 yoked light-flash study (Persinger et al. 2010: shared fields "based on 100ms"). The 2003 abstract names no other configuration; the lab's "standard protocol" table in the Swann paper also has a 200-ms rotation with "-2" (3-ms points, 3 s apart), which persinger-swann-2002-table1 runs. The order, three burst-firing then three frequency-modulated, follows the lab's six-configuration table in the Swann paper (Persinger et al. 2002) and Murphy's Shiva 'Published Studies' session; Murphy's three chirp phases are replaced by the lab's frequency-modulated Thomas pulse, played from its exact 849-point patent table. Point durations follow the Swann table, which prints 1-ms points with 1 ms between repeats for both 20+2 and 100 ms + 20 (rechecked on the page scan); 100+10 also runs at 1 ms, as in the lab's later shared-field work (Dotta & Persinger 2012). Burst-firing point values were never published; the built-in accelerating burst stands in as 230 points of 1 ms (the 6-30 Hz, 0.69-s sweep of the 3-ms Burst-X three times faster: 18 to 90 Hz in 0.23 s). The ring layout (Fpz, F7, T7, P7, Oz, P8, T8, F8, counter-clockwise from above) approximates the lab's eight solenoids in the horizontal plane, whose coil 1 sat over the left frontal and coil 8 over the right prefrontal region; persinger-siblings-2003-stimulus is a separate reconstruction on such a ring. The 2003 result rests on four sibling pairs in one lab, and the abstract and the 2010 retelling disagree on where it appeared (frontal and occipital versus right parietal). Independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). The sender/receiver framing is this project's trial design. Both partners must know about and agree to the experiment; score trials blind and never use them for decisions about real people. Not for people with epilepsy; stop on distress.
setting: Sender: seated in a quiet room with the helmet, looking at the target picture (in the 2003 study the stimulus person sat blindfolded in a closed chamber and imagined being in the other room touching the partner). Receiver: another room, no helmet, writing or sketching impressions (in 2003 blindfolded, 5 or 10 m away, with EEG). Use the app's blinded trial (hidden target, committed before the response, blind ranking against decoys).
schedule: At most weekly for the sender (Murphy's rule for Shiva sessions); the sibling pairs had two sessions a week apart.
